You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in space group number 46, Ima2 (Hall symbol I 2 -2a), using fractional coordinates. The original input cell is not the conventional orthorhombic cell: it is a rhombohedral-like cell with all three lattice parameters equal to 8.56472268 Å and interaxial angles α = 143.98265172°, β = 142.25921918°, and γ = 53.15680774°. This input cell contains 18 atoms with the declared composition Ca₄Co₄O₁₀.

The relation between the input and standard frames is q_standard = P q_input + s, where P has rows (0.5, 0.5, −0.5), (−0.5, 0.5, −0.5), and (−0.5, 0.5, 0.5), and the origin shift s is (0.0000005, 0.0000005, −0.0000005). This transformation must be applied to recover the standard setting from the original input cell.

In the standard frame, the calcium atoms occupy a single independent orbit on the general Wyckoff position 8c, with representative fractional coordinates (x, y, z) = (0.1105985, 0.5227235, 0.9582235); all three coordinates are independent and the multiplicity is eight. The cobalt atoms are distributed over two inequivalent orbits. One Co orbit lies on 4b with the coordinate relation (1/4, y, z), where y = 0.0586475 and z = 0.9904335. The second Co orbit lies on 4a with the coordinate relation (0, 0, z), where z = 0.9492225. Thus the four cobalt atoms in the input composition arise from two distinct fourfold sites.

The oxygen atoms occupy three independent orbits. The first is an 8c general position with representative coordinates (0.1421870, 0.5672000, 0.4256960). The second is a 4b site with fixed x = 1/4 and independent parameters y = 0.1159795 and z = 0.3564115. The third is another 8c general position with representative coordinates (0.0133700, 0.2472900, 0.2015450). Together these orbits account for the ten oxygen atoms in the input cell.

The input coordinates were rounded to six decimal places before correction, and small precision corrections are required to preserve the real input geometry rather than forcing it onto an idealized symmetry backbone. For calcium, the atom at input fractional position (0.412125, 0.847625, 0.480948) is displaced by (0, 0, −0.000001), and the calcium atom at (0.133322, 0.568822, 0.480948) is displaced by the same amount, (0, 0, −0.000001). For cobalt, the atom at (0.808647, 0.740434, 0.049082) is displaced by (0, 0, −0.000001); the atom at (0.191353, 0.240433, 0.931787) is displaced by (0, +0.000001, 0); the atom at (0.000000, 0.949223, 0.949224) is displaced by (0, 0, −0.000001); and the atom at (0.500000, 0.449222, 0.949223) is displaced by (0, +0.000001, 0).

The oxygen corrections are as follows. The oxygen atom at (0.425013, 0.283509, 0.992897) is displaced by (0, +0.000001, −0.000001). The atom at (0.209387, 0.067883, 0.992897) is displaced by (−0.000001, 0, −0.000001). The atom at (0.790613, 0.783509, 0.858497) is displaced by (+0.000001, +0.000001, 0). The atom at (0.134020, 0.606412, 0.240433) is displaced by (0, 0, −0.000002). The atom at (0.865980, 0.106411, 0.472392) is displaced by (0, +0.000001, 0). The atom at (0.766080, 0.214915, 0.954256) is displaced by (−0.000001, 0, −0.000001). The atom at (0.233920, 0.188175, 0.448836) is displaced by (+0.000001, +0.000001, 0). Finally, the oxygen atom at (0.239340, 0.688175, 0.954256) is displaced by (0, +0.000001, −0.000001).

Taken together, these lattice parameters, frame transformation, independent Wyckoff orbits, and explicit small corrections fully specify the three-dimensional atomic arrangement in the original input cell.
